gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Noto Sans Gothic opens its counters wide, like glass beads, with round forms that curve like parentheses. Noto Sans Gothic against Styro's crowded, nearly shut letters is the whole story: one huddles, the other breathes.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Styro packs its big lowercase so tight that the e and c almost seal shut. And Noto Sans Grantha, tall and nib-shaped, runs along beneath without ever catching on a closed-up bowl.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Styro crowds its letters together with retro swagger. Noto Sans Gujarati lets its curved strokes stop short of turning inward, so the large openings feel generous, while Styro earns its place when the words are big and brief.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-gondi: Styro presses its letters shoulder to shoulder, retro and bossy. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi has crayon-tall strokes and terminals cut back to leave big gaps, so the page moves from tight and heavy to loose and modern.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Styro brings a retro, commanding look, its lowercase large and its letters jammed nearly shut. But Noto Sans Gurmukhi turns its terminals outward like tongs, and that open, clean habit is the sharpest difference here.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Noto Sans Hanunoo reads easily, its lowercase filling nearly the full height and its terminals left open. Noto Sans Hanunoo gets more comfortable when given a little extra size, while Styro stays crowded and retro up top.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Styro is retro and crowded, almost shut. Its heading letters hit hard with a sizable lowercase, while Noto Sans Hebrew lets its huge midsection and wide gaps between curve ends and stems do the quiet, easy work.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-hk: Tight and loud, then wide and clear. Styro jams its letters together with a retro punch, and Noto Sans HK follows with large lowercase forms whose brush ends lift away before each curve closes.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-imperial-arama: Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic has a c whose ends point apart like open pincers, and its capitals barely rise above the lowercase. Give that body some extra size, and Styro's crowded, retro lettering will still dominate the heading.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-inscriptional-: Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian reads wide open, with big eyes on every e and a and a deep middle band. Nudge its size up a touch, and it will sit comfortably under Styro's crowded, retro heading.
